correctness.rationale: For each eigenpair the imaginary Rayleigh identity forces a real eigenmode to have zero center amplitude. The untouched half gives a simple Dirichlet eigenvalue, while evaluation of the left rank-one determinant at this energy forces an impurity node, exactly equivalent to divisibility, yielding the gcd count at arbitrary nonzero real detuning. Each unperturbed dark eigenvalue is simple in the full non-Hermitian matrix by an explicit parity/bright-block invertibility argument. The resolvent optical identity and explicitly solved center-source equation determine the imaginary second-order term without a weak-loss expansion. Normalization factors and signs are independently checked by directly built finite matrices (380 nonnode cases and all defect sites through half-length eight), with small-size exact symbolic characteristic-polynomial derivatives. The proof does not rely on finite tests.

originality.rationale: The detailed central-loss sources establish unperturbed odd modes and perturbative robustness of different steady-state quantities; they do not present the exact arithmetic survival classification for a single asymmetric local potential or the position-resolved linewidth coefficient for the one-particle no-jump spectrum. The second closely relevant primary manuscript addresses arbitrary pump/loss geometries and geometric resonances, not these single-defect spectral invariants. Published database searches for direct formulations and potentially dominating perturbation laws returned only distinct operator settings. General analytic perturbation and rank-one determinant formulas are methods and do not state the evaluated coefficient or arithmetic selection rule. Residual priority risk is recognized, and the novelty assessment does not follow merely from absent search results.

value.rationale: Loss-free dark-mode stability under a localized on-site detuning is a natural robustness question raised by central-loss spin-chain protocols. The theorem supplies a complete necessary/sufficient arithmetic selection rule at every nonzero defect strength and a nontrivial explicit decay-rate sensitivity for the unprotected resonances. Site dependence is quartic in the eigenfunction amplitude, with a sharp gamma-linear coefficient at fixed dissipation, distinguishing near-nodes from generic locations. These structural facts determine which localized defects preserve a dark subspace and quantitatively compare lifetimes; neither is a mere finite table or unmotivated exceptional example.
